task: Reverse-transfer release family 115 to a conditional randomization model for single-cell gene-by-cell counts, correcting the Poisson-uniformity boundary

claims.statement: The pinned family-115 source states that for nonnegative integer row and column margins with equal total, with complete support and no supplied cell caps, there is an exact uniform sampler terminating almost surely with expected bit cost polynomial in both dimensions and log of the total. It separately states a worst-case polynomial-bit sampler within 2^-k total variation, polynomial in dimensions, log total, and k.
assumptions: Complete cell support; no input forbidden positions or individual caps.
Margins are binary-encoded nonnegative integers with equal total.
Unbiased random bits and bit-operation cost model.
claims.status: source-reported theorem statement; relevant PDF statements/sections read, proof not independently verified, no implementation replay or external review
claims.novelty_boundary: Historical priority, correctness, and practical advantage are not independently established. Exact expected-time sampling has restricted-class primary antecedents, including Miller-Harrison and sparse-margin Arman-Gao-Wormald results.
claims.costs: Expected polynomial bit time in dimensions and log total; separate bounded-time sampler polynomial in accuracy bits k. The paper itself notes a rare exhaustive correction branch and deliberately large polynomial exponents. Dense table output costs at least one write per cell.
claims.falsifier: A proof error or an exhaustive small-instance check showing output support/probabilities disagree with uniformity; algorithmic cost claim requires independent proof review or reproducible implementation accounting.
claims.next_gate: Obtain independent proof review and implementation; benchmark on realistic single-cell dimensions without upgrading the source claim from its current status.

claims.statement: The pinned family-115 bounded-table source states an all-execution polynomial-bit FPRAS for counting nonnegative integer tables with arbitrary binary-encoded margins and individual upper bounds, including zero bounds/structural zeros. Its conditional-count self-reduction gives a sampler within TV tau of uniform, reports infeasibility exactly, and has all-execution polynomial-bit cost in input length and tau^-1. It does not claim exact sampling for arbitrary capped fibers.
assumptions: Margins and all cell upper bounds are explicit binary-encoded integers.
The feasible fiber may be empty; zero upper bounds encode forbidden positions.
FPRAS accuracy inputs epsilon, delta; sampling TV input tau.
claims.status: source-reported theorem statement; proof not independently verified
claims.novelty_boundary: Prior FPRAS results cover important special cases such as binary tables, fixed row dimension, and tight-capacity settings. Family 115 unrestricted correctness and priority remain unverified here.
claims.costs: Counting cost polynomial in total binary input length L, epsilon^-1, and log(delta^-1); approximate sampling cost polynomial in L and tau^-1 on every execution. A dense per-cell bound/mask requires O(rows times columns) input entries unless a supported sparse encoding is established.
claims.falsifier: A feasible bounded fiber where estimated count guarantee or self-reduction sampling guarantee fails; exact proof review needed beyond the stated theorem and inspected source sections.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof/code audit and realistic dense/sparse data benchmarks.

claims.statement: For independent Poisson cell counts with means lambda_gc=a_g b_c, conditioned on row and column margins and any fixed support/bounds, table probability is proportional to the product over cells of 1/x_gc!. It is uniform on a particular fiber if and only if the product of all cell factorials is constant on that fiber. Non-factorized means leave interaction weights as well.
assumptions: Independent Poisson variables on allowed cells.
Fixed row and column totals; fixed, data-independent support and cell bounds.
Factorized means lambda_gc=a_g b_c for the simple factorial-weighted formula.
claims.status: proved directly by conditioning the joint Poisson pmf; no external theorem needed
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical conditional-table calculation; no novelty claimed. It corrects the overbroad inference that Poisson conditioning gives uniform tables.
claims.costs: Constant-size symbolic derivation; no data acquisition. Using this law for inference requires a sampler for the factorial-weighted target if it is not the intended uniform microcanonical null.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic error in the conditional pmf; the exact 2x2 case in the linked script is a reproducible check of the nonuniformity claim.
claims.next_gate: If the scientific null is Poisson, compare/use its factorial-weighted conditional law rather than substituting the uniform sampler.

claims.statement: If independent nonnegative geometric cell counts have pmf (1-q_gc)q_gc^k with q_gc=a_g b_c in (0,1), conditioning on any fixed row/column margins gives the uniform law over the feasible tables. The result continues to hold on any fixed bounded/structural-zero fiber for appropriately truncated geometric variables. This is NB shape 1 and is overdispersed: variance equals mean plus mean squared.
assumptions: Independent cell counts with a fixed common geometric shape 1.
Geometric odds factor as a_g b_c on the allowed support.
Support and cell bounds are fixed independently of the observed random zeros; each q_gc is below one.
claims.status: proved by direct factorization on the fiber; model-scoped conditional-uniform bridge, not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The conditioning identity is standard exponential-family reasoning. The specific application is a clearly stated overdispersed gene-by-cell null; empirical fit and biological usefulness are UNKNOWN.
claims.costs: No estimation of a_g or b_c is required after conditioning. Unbounded complete-support sampling uses the family-115 exact sampler at source-reported expected polynomial cost; bounded/structural-zero sampling is only approximate via the separate family-115 bounded interface.
claims.falsifier: Two feasible tables with unequal conditional mass under the stated independent geometric/separable-odds model; direct factorization rules this out unless support or parameter assumptions fail.
claims.next_gate: Evaluate calibration on blinded negative controls and compare to Poisson and NB alternatives with the same margins.

claims.statement: For 2x2 margins (2,2)/(2,2), the fiber has three tables. Under factorized independent Poisson means their conditional probabilities are (1/6,2/3,1/6); under factorized independent NB shape 2 odds they are (9/34,16/34,9/34); under geometric/NB shape 1 they are (1/3,1/3,1/3).
assumptions: Three-table fiber described in the report.
Poisson or negative-binomial odds factor by row and column.
NB shape is common across cells.
claims.status: exact finite-rational check passed; proof follows from the conditional weights
claims.costs: Three feasible tables; exact rational arithmetic only.
claims.falsifier: The saved script asserts the fiber and all three probability vectors using fractions; changing a conditional law or margin is needed to produce a different result.
claims.next_gate: Use this as the minimal regression check when implementing a conditional sampler.

claims.statement: Under the independent geometric shape-1 model with gene-by-cell odds q_gc=a_g b_c, a raw gene-by-cell count table is uniform conditional on its gene totals and cell library totals. A prespecified gene-set versus cell-group association statistic can therefore be tested by exact fixed-margin randomization on the uncapped complete-support fiber; the plus-one Monte Carlo p-value is finite-sample superuniform. For caps/structural zeros, use only the bounded approximate sampler, with sampling-law error charged.
assumptions: Raw integer counts, fixed prespecified gene set and cell group, and no post-selection of support/masks from the tested zeros.
Independent geometric shape-1 counts with multiplicatively separable cell odds.
For the exact family-115 sampler: full support and no supplied cell caps; for capped fibers: source-reported bounded TV sampler only.
claims.status: conditional statistical validity proved under stated model; biological fit and actual dataset validation not performed
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific use of established fixed-margin randomization; no biological validation, causal interpretation, or novelty claim.
claims.costs: For M exact uncapped samples, expected source-theorem runtime is M times a polynomial in dimensions and log total, plus M statistic calculations; the statistic reads the gene-by-cell matrix. Additive Monte Carlo error eta at confidence 1-delta takes M at least log(2/delta)/(2 eta^2). For bounded approximate samples, choose per-sample tau at most tau_total/M and pay polynomial input-size and tau^-1 cost each sample.
claims.falsifier: Mis-calibration on blinded negative controls or clear departure from geometric conditional exchangeability; a failure of biology fit does not falsify the combinatorial family-115 theorem.
claims.next_gate: Run a preregistered negative-control/positive-control study with raw counts, donors, batches, spike-ins or technical replicates, comparing uniform, Poisson-factorial, and NB/capture-aware conditional nulls.

claims.statement: The reconstructed N77 network has infinitely many closed irreducible positive-recurrent classes in B+C=2 with pi_n(A at least n)=1, so the stationary family is not tight despite the shared positive ODE attractor. This is a classwise tightness obstruction only.
assumptions: Unit-rate N77 network and falling-factorial stochastic mass action as summarized in the pinned card.
claims.status: brief internally reconstructed carry-forward from supplied summary; full source proof/code packet absent and fixtures unreplayed
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim; retained only to preserve the negative observation while avoiding overlap with parent probability work.
claims.costs: No new derivation or experiment in this pivot.
claims.falsifier: Any enabled reaction escaping the stated class or a stationary law placing mass below A=n.

unknowns: Independent proof validation and implementation replay for the family-115 exact sampler, bounded FPRAS, and bounded near-uniform sampler.
Whether a particular single-cell dataset is adequately modeled by independent geometric/NB-shape-1 counts with separable gene and cell odds.
Whether donor, batch, cell-type, capture, ambient-RNA, dropout, and data-selection effects have been controlled sufficiently for a fixed-margin randomization null.
Practical runtimes, peak memory, and sparse-input/output behavior at realistic gene-by-cell dimensions; polynomial theorem bounds have large/unspecified exponents.
Whether family-115 result priority or novelty claims survive external literature review.
